claims.text: A 71-year-old woman, former smoker with 40 pack-years, had severe asthma-COPD overlap with predominant GOLD stage 3 COPD, allergic rhinitis and dust-mite/birch sensitization. Despite triple inhaled therapy including approximately 700 μg/day budesonide-equivalent ICS, she had four exacerbations yearly and progressive exertional dyspnea with marked quality-of-life impairment. Spirometry showed severe nonreversible obstruction; baseline FEV1 was 0.81 L with discrepant 39% versus 40% predicted wording. Plethysmography showed hyperinflation. Left-lower-lobe perfusion was 5% of total counts, with complete fissures and volumes 683 mL by StratX/669 mL by SPECT. A printed positive 910-HU threshold and swapped body/caption panel references require review. Low eosinophils/IgE were reported, with conflicting narrative/table units. No long-term corticosteroids were reported alongside documented inhaled ICS. Tezepelumab began in November 2022; after two doses, at an unreported response date, dyspnea and overall condition improved. BLVR in February 2023 placed six left-lower-lobe valves without complications. Serial measurements cover 1.5 years, six months and one month before tezepelumab, then four weeks, 12 months and 24 months after BLVR. At 12 months FEV1 was 1.06 L/55% predicted, SGRQ 17, CAT 11 and mMRC 1; at 24 months FEV1 was 0.96 L/51%, RV 2.21 L/115% and six-minute walking distance 405 m. Narrative two-year follow-up reports sustained benefit and exacerbations reduced to two yearly; the claimed 63-point SGRQ reduction at two years is not corroborated by the blank 24-month SGRQ cell. Individual effects of biologic and BLVR cannot be separated from this sequential course.

evidence.quote: A 71‐year‐old woman, ex‐smoker (40 pack‐years), was diagnosed with ACO with a predominant COPD component classified as Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease Stage 3. Her history included allergic rhinitis, with onset in early adulthood, characterised by sensitisation to dust mites and birch pollen, and seasonal rhinoconjunctivitis. Despite maximal inhaled therapy, corresponding to an inhaled corticosteroid dose of approximately 700 μg budesonide equivalent per day, she experienced four exacerbations annually and progressive exertional dyspnea severely limiting her quality of life.
